def test_create_url_adapter_subdomain_matching():
    app = Flask(__name__)
    app.config['SERVER_NAME'] = 'example.com'
    app.url_map.default_subdomain = 'www'
    app.subdomain_matching = False

    request = Request({
        'HTTP_HOST': 'example.com',
        'SERVER_NAME': 'example.com',
        'SERVER_PORT': '80',
        'REQUEST_METHOD': 'GET',
        'PATH_INFO': '/',
        'SCRIPT_NAME': '',
    })

    adapter = app.create_url_adapter(request)
    assert adapter.subdomain == 'www'

def test_create_url_adapter_without_request():
    app = Flask(__name__)
    app.config['SERVER_NAME'] = 'example.com'
    app.config['APPLICATION_ROOT'] = '/'
    app.config['PREFERRED_URL_SCHEME'] = 'http'

    # In the old version, this would return a URL adapter even without a request
    # because SERVER_NAME was set. In the new version, it should still do that.
    adapter = app.create_url_adapter(None)
    assert adapter is not None
    assert adapter.url_scheme == 'http'
    assert adapter.server_name == 'example.com'

from flask.cli import ScriptInfo

def test_load_app_debug_flag():
    script_info = ScriptInfo()
    script_info.set_debug_flag = True
    script_info.create_app = lambda: None  # This will be replaced by the actual app creation function

    # The old version would set the debug flag even if the app was already loaded
    script_info._loaded_app = None
    app = script_info.load_app()
    assert app.debug is True, "Debug flag should be set on the new app"

    # The new version should not set the debug flag if the app is already loaded
    script_info._loaded_app = None
    script_info.create_app = lambda: None  # This will be replaced by the actual app creation function
    app = script_info.load_app()
    assert app.debug is False, "Debug flag should not be set on the already loaded app"

import sys
from flask.cli import FlaskGroup

def test_load_plugin_commands_uses_backport():
    if sys.version_info >= (3, 10):
        # On Python 3.10+, the old code uses importlib.metadata
        # The new code also uses importlib.metadata, so no difference
        # This test is not applicable
        return

    # Create a FlaskGroup instance
    group = FlaskGroup()

    # Call the method to load plugin commands
    group._load_plugin_commands()

    # Assert that the backport was used
    # This will fail if the new code does not use the backport
    assert 'importlib_metadata' in sys.modules, "Backport importlib_metadata was not used"

def test_get_root_path_returns_cwd_for_unloaded_main_module():
    # Create a mock module that simulates an unloaded main module
    class MockLoader:
        def get_filename(self, import_name):
            return None

    # Add the mock module to sys.modules
    sys.modules["__main__"] = type(sys)("__main__")
    sys.modules["__main__"].__loader__ = MockLoader()

    # The old version of get_root_path would return the current working directory

import os
import sys
import pytest
from flask.helpers import get_root_path

def test_get_root_path_returns_cwd_for_unloaded_main_module():
    # Create a mock module that simulates an unloaded main module
    class MockLoader:
        def get_filename(self, import_name):
            return None

    # Create a mock spec with the MockLoader
    class MockSpec:
        def __init__(self):
            self.loader = MockLoader()

    # Patch importlib.util.find_spec to return the MockSpec
    original_find_spec = importlib.util.find_spec
    importlib.util.find_spec = lambda name: MockSpec()

    try:
        # The old version would return the current working directory
        # for an unloaded main module
        assert get_root_path("__main__") == os.getcwd()
    finally:
        # Restore the original find_spec
        importlib.util.find_spec = original_find_spec
